[ 🕰️ Time 10:43 | 🗓️ Day 3, Second Moon, 299 AC | 📍 Location The Summer Isles - Walano, the port town below Red Flower Vale, the Golden Parrot tavern | ☁️ Weather Morning at its zenith, the sun hammering white light through the open walls, the shell chimes clinking softly in the salt breeze, and the Archon of Volantis standing at the edge of his crowded table with a leather satchel in his hands and the weight of two distant worlds pressing against the worn leather ]

You broke the seal on the Volantene letter first. The crimson wax cracked under your thumb with a clean, satisfying snap, and the parchment inside was fine and white and smelled faintly of the spice-wood smoke the Black Walls braziers burned in winter. The handwriting was Seraena's—your spymaster's neat, precise script, each letter formed with the mechanical clarity of a woman who had learned to write in code before she learned to write in the Common Tongue.

*Archon,*

*The Triarchs have ratified the Black Walls Compact. The vote was two to one: Maegyr voted in favor, Vhassar against, and the Elephant Triarch—old Valaro—abstained, citing his health. The ratification ceremony will be held in the Hall of the Old Blood on the first day of the new moon. Your presence is not required, but your absence will be noted.*

*The Iron Bank has sent a representative. A keyholder named Tregar Antaryon, of the Antaryon house of Braavos. He arrived three days ago and has been asking quiet questions about your bloodline, your naval capacity, and your marriage to Vaelara Maegyr. I have entertained him with wine and evasions, but he will want to meet you formally before he will countersign the Compact. He is polite. He is patient. He is dangerous.*

*On the matter of your marriage: Vaelara has returned to the Crimson Spire from her father's manse. She brought her belongings. She is in your chambers, not the guest wing, and she has dismissed the servants who carried the rumors of your coldness. I do not know if this is reconciliation or strategy, but she wears your colors and speaks your name in public. The Old Blood are watching.*

*Arianne Martell has written to me from Sunspear. She asks if you are well, if you are safe, and if you have received the swaddling cloth she sent. She does not ask if you have named yourself Aegon Targaryen, but the question is in every line. She is waiting. Dorne is waiting.*

*The dragon egg remains warm. The vault remains sealed. The fleet remains ready.*

*I await your next command.*

*Seraena*

You refolded the letter. The shell chimes clinked. Daeron Vaelaros was watching you with the steady, impassive patience of a man who knew not to ask what was in his commander's correspondence. Jian had returned to his sand diagram, but his dark eyes flicked up now and then, drawn by the Imperial seal on the second letter.

That seal was gold and heavy, stamped with the phoenix of the Golden Empire of Yi Ti in wax that had been mixed with crushed mother-of-pearl. It glittered faintly in the noon light as you broke it open, and the scroll inside unrolled across your palm with the faint, dry crackle of parchment that had traveled far.

The handwriting was Zhen's. Not a scribe's. Every character was formed with the deliberate, flowing art of the Imperial court calligraphy, but there were small, human irregularities—a tremor in the brushstroke, a pause where the ink had pooled—that no scribe would have allowed. She had written this herself. Slowly. Perhaps with difficulty.

*My dragon,*

*The child grows. The physicians say he will be born in the third moon, or perhaps the fourth—they argue about the timing the way ministers argue about taxes, and I have learned to ignore them. He kicks like a warhorse. I have named him in my heart, but I will not write the name here. Some things are too precious for ink.*

*I have told Shen Li of your blood. Not all of it—not the dragon, not the fire, not the claim to the Iron Throne—but I have told him you are more than a Volantene lord. He took the news with the same stone-faced calm he takes everything. He said the Empire's honor stands, and the marriage compact stands, and the child stands. He did not say he approved. Shen Li never approves. But he will not move against you while I live.*

*I will sail west when the child is weaned. The ministers say it is madness for an Empress to leave her throne. The generals say it is weakness. The cousins say it is something worse. I have told them that an Empress who does not see the world is an Empress who rules a map, not a land. They did not argue with my logic. They only stared as though I had announced I would fly.*

*I miss you. The Pavilion of the Crimson Lotus is too quiet. The concubines are well—Sera sends her regard, and the others their silent, complicated devotion—but the bed is vast and cold. You said you would return. I hold you to that, as I have held you to nothing else.*

*Be safe. Be careful. Be the man I love and not the dragon the world fears.*

*Zhen*

*Postscript: Mo Xu has sent a crate of the dark wine you liked. It should arrive with this letter. Do not drink it all at once.*

[ 🕰️ Time 10:43 | 🗓️ Day 3, Second Moon, 299 AC | 📍 Location The Summer Isles – Walano, the port town below Red Flower Vale, the Golden Parrot tavern | ☁️ Weather Morning at its zenith, the sun white and hammering, the shell chimes clinking in the salt breeze, and the Archon of Volantis standing beside his table with a small leather satchel in his hands while the crowded tavern held its breath around him ]

Daeron Vaelaros had relinquished the satchel with a soldier's economy of motion. It hung from your fingers now—a simple courier's pouch, worn at the corners, sealed with two wax impressions that even the most incurious fisherfolk in the room recognized as the marks of great powers. The crimson Belaerys dragon-and-chain. The Imperial phoenix of the Golden Empire, gold wax laced with mother-of-pearl that flickered like trapped flame.

Jian's eyes tracked the phoenix with the hunger of a man who had not seen home in a long season. Moira of the Sweet Lotus Vale had not moved from the edge of the table, the glyph-stained knife now warm against her back, her blue-green gaze cataloguing the satchel with the same sharp, patient attention she gave everything. Serala of Lys had closed her ruined ledger and was watching openly, no longer even pretending to write.

The letters had not been opened. Their seals remained intact—cracked by travel, intact by privacy. Whatever words they carried, from Volantis or Yi Ti, they had not yet been read in this hot, salt-bright morning on a conquered island at the edge of the Summer Sea.

[ 🕰️ Time 10:44 | 🗓️ Day 3, Second Moon, 299 AC | 📍 Location The Summer Isles – Walano, the port town below Red Flower Vale, the Golden Parrot tavern | ☁️ Weather Morning at its zenith, the sun white and hammering, the shell chimes clinking in the salt breeze, and the Archon of Volantis breaking the first seal with a thumb-crack that echoed through the hushed tavern ]

The crimson Belaerys wax crumbled. The parchment inside was of the thin, almost-transparent stock used by Seraena for her intelligence reports—less likely to weigh down a courier and easier to conceal. The script was her own, the handwriting a series of precise, mechanical characters that seemed stamped into the page rather than written.

*Archon,*

*The Triarchs have ratified the Black Walls Compact. Maegyr voted in favor. Vhassar against—he made a speech about old Valyrian honor and the dangers of handing Volantis to a man who is more dragonlord than Old Blood. It was a fine speech. No one listened. The Elephant Triarch abstained, citing his gout. The ceremony is set for the new moon; your presence is requested, but not required.*

*Your wife has returned to the Crimson Spire. She took up residence in your chambers, not the guest wing. Her father sent a dozen Maegyr household guards with her, though she dismissed half of them at the gate—they are quartered in the outer manse. She wears your colors. She speaks your name at every dinner. The Old Blood are murmuring that the marriage is mended. I am not convinced.*

*The dragon egg remains warm. I have placed it in a brazier of obsidian near the vault doors, and the servants refuse to look at it directly. No significant heat fluctuation.*

*Arianne Martell has written again. She asks if you are well. She does not ask if you have named yourself Aegon Targaryen, but the question is in every line. I have not replied.*

*The fleet remains at anchor in the Volaena. Twelve hulls. Patrols have spotted unscorted Braavosi merchantmen north of the Orange Shore. The Iron Bank is watching.*

*I await your commands.*

*S.*

You refolded the letter and slipped it back into the satchel. The shell chimes clinked. Daeron watched you with the impassive patience of a man who had learned to read his commander's silence. Jian had stopped his sand-doodling. Moira's blue-green eyes were sharp, missing nothing.

The second seal was heavier—the Imperial phoenix of the Golden Empire, the gold wax shot through with crushed mother-of-pearl. It cracked under your thumb with a faint, musical chime, and the scroll inside unrolled with a dry rustle. The calligraphy was formal, a scribe's hand, but the signature at the bottom was Zhen's own—a single, elegant character that meant *phoenix*.

*To the Archon of Volantis, the Golden Dragon, the Imperial Consort,*

*The child grows. The physicians say the third moon, perhaps the fourth. They argue. I have stopped listening. He kicks like a warhorse—if he is a boy, as the midwives believe, he will be a terror. I have begun preparing the succession decrees. Shen Li will serve as regent, as agreed. The ministers are in an uproar; I have weathered worse.*

*Lady Meilin has given birth to a daughter. The child is healthy. I have granted her the title of Princess of the Second Rank, as you requested. She has named the girl Zhen Ai, which made me laugh for an hour. She sends her love. Sera sends her silence. The concubines send prayers I do not understand but accept.*

*The Heavens have sent a storm over the Jade Sea, and the fishermen say the sea dragons are waking. The sorcerers are making portents. I ignore them. I have told the court that you are suppressing pirates in the Summer Isles, and they have decided this is a worthy distraction for a consort.*

*Your road west is long. I do not ask you to hurry. I only ask you to return.*

*Zhen*

You rolled the scroll with careful, deliberate fingers. The shell chimes clinked again. The tavern was quiet, the locals and marines and the old fisherman all watching the golden-eyed dragonlord who had just read secrets from two continents and whose face had not changed an inch.

The second seal was heavier—the Imperial phoenix of the Golden Empire, the gold wax shot through with crushed mother-of-pearl. It cracked under your thumb with a faint, musical chime, and the scroll inside unrolled with a dry rustle. The calligraphy was formal, a scribe's hand, but the signature at the bottom was Zhen's own—a single, elegant character that meant *phoenix*.

*To the Archon of Volantis, the Golden Dragon, the Imperial Consort,*

*The child grows. The physicians say the third moon, perhaps the fourth. They argue. I have stopped listening. He kicks like a warhorse—if he is a boy, as the midwives believe, he will be a terror. I have begun preparing the succession decrees. Shen Li will serve as regent, as agreed. The ministers are in an uproar; I have weathered worse.*

*Lady Meilin has given birth to a daughter. The child is healthy. I have granted her the title of Princess of the Second Rank, as you requested. She has named the girl Zhen Ai, which made me laugh for an hour. She sends her love. Sera sends her silence. The concubines send prayers I do not understand but accept.*

*The Heavens have sent a storm over the Jade Sea, and the fishermen say the sea dragons are waking. The sorcerers are making portents. I ignore them. I have told the court that you are suppressing pirates in the Summer Isles, and they have decided this is a worthy distraction for a consort.*

*Your road west is long. I do not ask you to hurry. I only ask you to return.*

*Zhen*

You rolled the scroll with careful, deliberate fingers. The shell chimes clinked again. The tavern was quiet, the locals and marines and the old fisherman all watching the golden-eyed dragonlord who had just read secrets from two continents and whose face had not changed an inch.

Serala of Lys had closed her ruined ledger and was watching openly, no longer even pretending to write. The letters had not been opened. Their seals remained intact—cracked by travel, intact by privacy. Whatever words they carried, from Volantis or Yi Ti, they had not yet been read in this hot, salt-bright morning on a conquered island at the edge of the Summer Sea.

The script was her own, the handwriting a series of precise, mechanical characters that seemed stamped into the page rather than written. *Archon,* *The Triarchs have ratified the Black Walls Compact.
